issue.title: STAGE 02 — Imported Assets & Alpha Vegetation (Godot 4.7.2)
issue.body:
# GO_FLORA — STAGE 02: Imported Assets & Alpha Vegetation

**PROJECT:** GO_FLORA  
**REPOSITORY:** https://github.com/alekseypilishkov-gif/go_flora  
**STAGE:** 02 — Imported Assets & Alpha Vegetation  
**BASE BRANCH:** `main` (accepted Stage 01 merged via PR #4 at `5c076153e1dea6363b885e82f4ef391808586348`)  
**WORKING BRANCH:** `codex/stage-02-imported-alpha` (create fresh from latest `main`)  
**ENGINE BASELINE:** Godot **4.7.2**, initially Windows x86_64; preserve tested rendering paths  
**ARCHITECTURE:** ADR 0001 / ADR A, GDScript EditorPlugin, versioned logical placement records, transient spatial MultiMesh caches, optional providers  
**LICENSE:** Original code/docs MIT; only original or explicitly redistributable test assets  
**SCOPE:** Implement Stage 02 only. **NO automatic merge, public release, or Stage 03.**

## Goal and user workflow

Make GO_FLORA usable with real project vegetation instead of only Stage 01's placeholder cone and cube:

1. Add an existing user **Mesh** or imported **GLB** / **PackedScene** as a vegetation source, with accurate materials, transforms and deterministic placement.
2. Create a **grass/flower/fern/small-plant asset from a user-supplied transparent PNG/WebP** or selected atlas region, using simple single/crossed/radial cards with ground pivot.
3. Mix those sources in weighted `VegetationSet` palettes and use existing **Paint / Erase / Single**, Undo/Redo, persistent layer records and per-set **Draw distance (m)** to populate surfaces.
4. Allow a safe **scene-instance fallback** when a scene cannot be faithfully converted to shared static MultiMesh parts. Never silently discard authored gameplay components.

The product remains terrain-independent and useful with no Tree3D installation. **This is asset interchange and alpha cards, not the standalone Tree3D procedural generator.**

## Mandatory repository context

Read at least:
- `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, root `README.md`, `LICENSE`
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE_ADR_0001.md`, `docs/STAGE_01_DATA_CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/LICENSING_DECISION.md`
- `stages/01_painter_mvp/report.md`, `stages/01_painter_mvp/updates/02_dock_width_distance/report.md`
- `addons/go_flora/` including `data/source.gd`, `vegetation_layer_3d.gd`, `rendering/cell_renderer.gd`, editor `plugin.gd`, `core/placement.gd`
- Stage 01 tests, package/update tools and `stages/01_painter_mvp/manual_qa.md`.

Stage 01 **owner-accepted** core GUI workflow. Some wider manual-matrix/GPU/clean-export cases remain `NOT_RUN` and must not be retroactively relabeled. Historical Stage 00/01 directories are immutable evidence; new Stage 02 files go under `stages/02_imported_alpha_vegetation/`. Preserve Stage 01's deterministic ID/record format, and current local `TEST_FLORA` layout preferences.

## A — Compatibility and data contracts

1. Extend `GFVegetationSource` through an explicit **source resolver** with typed status, diagnostics, resource references, provider/source revision and capabilities. Preserve **existing enum numeric values, IDs and serialized Stage 01 files**. Do not silently reinterpret old `SCENE_UNSUPPORTED` or `GENERATED_UNSUPPORTED` values. If a source kind or record schema changes, introduce an explicit versioned migration verified on copies; no in-place destructive rewrite.
2. One logical record may yield **multiple static mesh parts** (one imported plant can contain several meshes/surfaces with local transforms/materials), or a managed scene-instance fallback. Keep logical records/transform/seed authoritative and renderer nodes disposable.
3. Distinguish shared static source parts from scene instances with authored behavior. Preserve material priority (mesh surface vs mesh-instance surface overrides vs material override), pivot and accumulated node transforms, normals/tangent behavior and UVs. **Never mutate source Mesh, original imported material or texture** to build a derived variant.
4. Invalid/missing resource, changed file, future schema, unsupported animation/skeleton/skin/script/scene feature: report the exact reason; keep logical records and IDs; offer fallback or explicit unsupported state without crash/deletion. No arbitrary path traversal or modification outside the Godot project.
5. Existing Stage 01 demo and accepted Paint/Erase/Single, Undo/Redo, per-set draw distance and scene roundtrip must remain functional. Keep `VegetationSet` and record semantics stable.

## B — Imported GLB/PackedScene classification

Develop a resolver/classifier, not a "first mesh found" shortcut:

- **Static-only case:** recognise imported GLB/GLTF and `PackedScene` hierarchies containing ordinary `Node3D` and `MeshInstance3D` static components; gather all eligible mesh parts with full accumulated transforms, per-surface effective materials, correct bounds, stable source part IDs. Verify real imported `.glb` through Godot's import pipeline.
- **Scene semantics:** if the scene has scripts, animation players, skeleton/skin, particles, lights, authored colliders, signals or other interactive parts, do not silently flatten them. Provide an explicit, capability-reported **scene-instance fallback** that preserves authored behavior/colliders for supported examples; show warning that scene instances are not MultiMesh and may be expensive. Treat arbitrary unsafe/unsupported scenes as unsupported until reviewed instead of pretending they were preserved. Avoid executing unknown user scripts merely to calculate a static source preview. Prefer safe validation before instantiation.
- For scene-instance fallback, maintain node ownership/lifecycle, placement mapping, set visibility/draw-distance policy **without silently disabling gameplay processing**. Handle edit-mode vs runtime capabilities explicitly. If an effect cannot be supported safely, surface a diagnostic and leave persisted records intact. Include one simple original scene-with-collider/script example and prove no authored semantic loss.
- Existing direct static Mesh source still takes the original fast path.
- Never copy upstream paid/demo GLB/texture assets into the public plugin. Demo files must be self-created and clearly licensed.

## C — Texture-based grass and small plants

Add a user-friendly creation workflow (dock/editor action plus editable resource/Inspector), minimally:

1. User selects a project-local **PNG/WebP Texture2D with transparency**; preview shows the source and UV/atlas region. Support standalone image and a **selected region from an atlas** (explicit pixel or normalized rectangle, documented), with validation against image dimensions and a configurable gutter/padding policy.
2. Geometry modes: **single upright card**, **two crossed cards**, and **configurable 3–4 radial/cross cards** (bounded mesh complexity). Expose plant width, height, card count, optional simple tilt/splay and **ground pivot**. The source stays deterministic; do not create a novel random mesh per painted instance.
3. Generate ordinary Godot Mesh + UVs + effective owned material(s), with appropriate double-sided rendering, alpha texture and cutout. The resulting resource must be reusable in multiple VegetationSets and paintable via existing brush.
4. **Alpha-scissor is default**, with adjustable threshold. Do not silently enable alpha-hash on Compatibility: Stage 00's alpha-hash test **FAIL** there. An optional alternative transparency mode may be included only behind renderer-specific evidence and explicit settings. Preserve alpha on import; avoid opaque quads, black halos, obvious atlas bleeding, reversed UVs and incorrect sorting assumptions.
5. Color/size/yaw variation remains provided by Stage 01 instance transforms. Do not overwrite vertex colors reserved for potential future wind data; actual wind is Stage 04.
6. User image ownership: asset references project files; generated materials/meshes are explicitly owned/cacheable and saved without changing the user’s originals. Change/reimport of source texture should invalidate material/mesh cache but **not regenerate logical instance positions**.

A procedural **geometric blade/grass modeler**, flower modeling, particle wind and biome ecology are OUT OF SCOPE. "Grass generation" here means alpha-card plant creation from a provided texture/atlas.

## D — Painter, batching and visibility integration

- All newly supported static Mesh parts and alpha-card sources must work with existing **Paint, Erase, Single, weighted palettes, deterministic seed, brush masks/slope/height, per-stroke Undo/Redo, cancellation and saved records**.
- For static multi-part sources, batch by layer, set, spatial cell, source/part revision, Mesh, effective material and LOD placeholder. One record may contribute transforms to several batches; erase/undo must remove/restore **all** associated parts. No orphan meshes after repeated edit/cancel.
- Ensure `Draw distance (m)` directly under the active set selection applies to **existing** batches from cards/imported meshes and supported fallback scene parts, `0` = unlimited. Changing A must not affect B or placement IDs/count/transforms. The draw distance applies to renderer cells; don't claim per-instance MultiMesh culling.
- For scene fallback, rendering visibility and gameplay lifecycle must be separated or explicitly limited. Do not hide/stop authored scripts/colliders as an accidental side effect of set distance.
- Preserve original editor usability: GO_FLORA dock **no min-height expansion or shifting width** (Stage 01 regression gates: approx 120 px minimum height / stable 260 px width), no interference with FileSystem, Output, Godot camera navigation. **Do not force a new dock layout or overwrite user's saved local TEST_FLORA layout**; packaged default follows accepted Stage 01 behavior unless the owner separately changes it.
- Keep bounded per-stroke work; source import must not freeze the editor unexpectedly. Record actual timing/memory where feasible. Full incremental dirty-cell optimization remains Stage 04.

## E — Acceptance and testing

**Stage 01 regression MUST PASS** first and last; do not weaken original tests.

Add deterministic automated tests and Godot native integration checks for:
1. Existing Stage 01 static resources and saved pre-Stage-02 scenes reopen with identical record IDs/transforms and per-set visibility behavior.
2. A real original `.glb` fixture imported through Godot, with multiple meshes/surfaces, nontrivial nested transforms and distinct materials; verify all parts, UVs, bounds and source immutability.
3. A static-only `PackedScene` resolved to shareable parts, and a mixed authored scene handled by supported scene fallback or blocked with precise diagnostic **without data loss**. Do not label unsupported as working fallback.
4. Single card, 2 crossed cards, 3–4 radial: counts, vertex normals, UV winding, ground pivot, aspect/size; standalone PNG/WebP alpha and atlas region UV mapping; invalid/out-of-bounds atlas rejected.
5. Real GPU pixel/screenshot tests for **alpha-scissor** on Compatibility, Mobile and Forward+ when available, with transparent texels revealing known background. Record hardware/backend. Verify texture filtering/mipmaps and atlas gutters at representative distances; alpha-hash Compatibility remains a documented known issue, not false PASS.
6. Paint/Erase/Single, preview, scene-bound Undo/Redo with each source kind; one record can yield multiple static parts; no orphan cache nodes.
7. Batch/cell behaviour and per-set draw-distance changes after placement for new source types; set B unchanged, authoritative records untouched; saved editor/runtime reload.
8. Resource reimport, missing texture or GLB, invalid scene, corrupted/future schema, unsupported source types: never delete or rewrite saved logical data; actionable diagnostics.
9. Resource/material ownership and no unintended mutation of user's original imported Mesh/material/Texture2D; renderer flags and no forced global project settings.
10. Repeated installation from **plugin-only ZIP**, CRC/digests, standalone-import/runtime smoke in a disposable Godot project and a copy of an existing Stage 01 QA scene. Existing scene's SHA must remain unchanged under the installer. Never test destructive update directly on owner's working project.
11. Benchmark moderate, explicitly counted patches (e.g. 1,000/5,000 cards or imported parts) and report CPU cache timings plus actual renderer observation if tested. Do not imply validated large-forest GPU/FPS optimization.

**Owner GUI review — mandatory before merge**:
- In a separate QA scene, select user PNG/WebP, create a single and crossed alpha-card, paint mixed grass/flower sources on both regular and tilted collision surfaces.
- Import a real GLB and a safe PackedScene; draw and inspect multi-part plants. Confirm materials, UV/transparency and ground placement visually.
- Erase selected set; Single click; undo/redo; Esc cancel and scene save/close/reopen; resource reimport retains positions.
- Test A/B draw-distance changes **after painting**, with camera near/far, including restored scene and `0` unlimited.
- Dock width/height remains stable; file browser, Output, viewport camera usable.

If actual interactive mouse/render GUI cannot be controlled by Codex, report `INTERACTIVE_GUI_QA: NOT_RUN` and `READY_FOR_MANUAL_QA`; supply reproduction steps, don't invent screenshots/video. Source analysis, headless API, GPU render and owner GUI each get distinct statuses.

## F — Packaging and deliverables

- New functional code under `addons/go_flora/{sources,data,editor,rendering,core}` and optional focused helpers. No native dependency required.
- New source docs under `docs/STAGE_02_*.md` / update `docs/ROADMAP.md` and README. Preserve and extend `docs/STAGE_01_DATA_CONTRACTS.md` with a Stage 02 addendum rather than changing historical facts.
- Dedicated `stages/02_imported_alpha_vegetation/` with `report.md` **in Russian**, `demo/` with originally generated fixtures (including real imported GLB + alpha textures), `manual_qa.md`, and `evidence/` containing exact commands, logs, source/content hashes and actual screenshots when available.
- `tests/` expanded; CI extended with Stage 02 relevant checks; preserve distinction between static, headless Godot and manual GUI gates.
- **Reproducible plugin-only ZIP**, source/manifest/checksums and update script **preserving the owner's scenes**. Preferred version `0.2.0-dev` if compatible with existing versioning; state exact shipped version.
- User's separate test project `C:\Dev\TEST_FLORA`: **do not modify, install or overwrite it automatically** during development. Use isolated copies, provide an optional owner-invoked install/update path, and keep backups. Respect saved dock arrangement (right next to Inspector in owner's local project).
- Work on `codex/stage-02-imported-alpha`, commit/push and open ONE focused PR to `main`. Link this Issue and evidence.
- No force-push, no unrelated project edits, no auto-merge, no release publication, no Stage 03. No Tree3D source/binaries/assets bundled or adapted here.

## Stage 02 exit conditions

A user can **import an actual GLB**, create a small foliage asset from their own **transparent PNG/WebP or atlas**, paint both into a saved scene, change per-set draw distances, undo/redo, reopen without losing instance records, and distribute the base addon without third-party dependency. Explicit fallback behavior and limitations are documented and verified.

Stop after a PR and report for owner review. Stage 03 (optional Tree3D generated trees/shrubs), Stage 04 (LOD/large forest/wind) and public release remain separate decisions.
